note: A sea backdrop derives every area's origin from the piece set it seats — `walk_ref_y - walk_y`, one block above the water — so it is a different world for the same campaign and cannot coexist with `void`. It builds from the SHORE set: the same hall and the same annex tiles lifted onto two courses of plinth, with a tide pool cut into the floor course so each piece's top water block lands on the sea plane and `waterline_y` can say so, and each declaring the walk plane its own bytes stand a body on (`walk_y: 3`, so the area is seated at 60 and the floor is dry at 63). It is the only point of this domain where the sea proofs have anything to look at: `validation/fluid-escape.json` (`DW0318`, water that leaves the built volume), `validation/sea-seepage.json` (`DW0851`, the sea in the walk region, measured over every walk cell), the `DW0344` waterline binding and its walk-plane arm all ship here with real denominators. `area/quay` is what makes the last of them non-vacuous: the other four pieces are sealed boxes whose outside no body can reach, so the sea's own power to bury an outward face — the thing that makes `ocean` seat a keep at all — was asserted nowhere and the exposure binding read `0 judged`. The quay is an open court on the same plinth, so the party's air runs around the outside of it: the plinth stands below y=62 and the WATER buries it, the parapet stands above it and the piece answers for it in `shown_faces`, and the point now reports 60 judged cells over 4 sides seen against 4 declarations of which 4 are bound.
